1:00 AM
Find a Startup to Help or Join

**Welcome!**

The official registration page is [here](Startupoasisvirtual.eventbrite.com).

If you are a developer, UX designer, marketer, or anyone else in the tech ecosystem looking to join or help a tech startup, or even just get involved in a project, this event is for you!

We will be introducing projects for you to get involved with during the pitches. There is no group like this on Meetup or in the startup world because we filter out the BS and get you going on a project ASAP.

(Stay inside the Startup Oasis by joining our [newsletter](https://mailchi.mp/startupoasis/meetup)!)

What happens first in the event is startup founders pitch their business or idea to the audience, which is full of the developers, designers, marketers, etc.

If you are interested in one of the projects / startups, you can join one of the founders in a breakout room to continue building, workshopping, and/or onboarding the startup with attendees.

People have been able to start and advance their businesses as a result of this process.

We are meeting on Zoom, the link is here in the listing.

**Agenda:**
**Intros:** During the first 10 minutes, we will give you the history, structure, and future plans of Startup Oasis and open signups for founders that want to pitch their startups.

**Pitches:** Each founder will then get up to 3 minutes to pitch their startup. This format is recommended: name, business, the problem, your solution, target customer base, and your biggest challenge/current need. This part is similar to Shark Tank.

**Breakout Groups:** For the remainder of the event, each founder gets a breakout room, and you can talk to the founders in greater detail about their needs and challenges in a small group setting. This part is similar to a hackathon.

Startup Oasis was created to pierce the illusion of accessibility of startups and tech by creating a grassroots forum for early-stage founders to pitch to those in the tech ecosystem to get real-time feedback for their idea or business.

Use this [link](https://lnk.bio/startup.oasis) to:

* Follow us on LinkedIn
* Join our community on Discord
* Donate to our cause
* Visit our website

**FAQ:**
**Is this event free to attend?** Yes - Startup Oasis will always be free for anyone to attend. If you would like to donate, you can do so directly on our [website](https://donate.stripe.com/eVa2a0dV27Nlb2ofYY). You can also talk to us about volunteer or sponsorship opportunities.

**How do I sign up to pitch?** RSVP here. Right when the event starts, fill out the form and then raise your hand on Zoom. That will also determine the order. You can also buy a VIP ticket to support our cause and guarantee you a spot to pitch. To be eligible to pitch, you must be the cofounder of a technology-based startup. Agencies, consultants, coaches, MLM schemes, and nonprofits are not eligible to pitch, but you can still watch the pitches and join the breakouts.

**What happens after the pitches?** The breakout groups open for the remainder of the event. Each founder gets a breakout room, and you can talk more about their business and needs with them.

**Can I invite other people that I know?** Yes - please have them RSVP here or on the [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/startup-oasis-global) event listing.

**How do I get the most out of this event?**

* Founders - In this event, no money is awarded nor are any winners named. We are not here to critique your pitch, just to help you find teammates, cofounders, and feedback from other professionals. Make sure your pitch is 3 minutes or less and clear about what your biggest needs are.
* Attendees - If you are new to startups and tech, feel free to just watch with no pressure to participate. If you are looking to join a startup or find a side project, make sure you take notes during the pitches to join the group of the founder that you're most interested in helping. Most founders need help with either developing the product or with a go-to-market strategy.
*

**Do we meet in person?** We do this event in Atlanta, GA each month in Midtown at ATDC.

**Content:** We are looking for founders to be interviewed or people to interview founders for short videos. Let us know if you are interested!

threadHOURS® at TouchPoint - Ongoing

Every Wednesday | 3-6 pm
Location:
TouchPoint: 3201 Tioga Parkway, Suite P, Baltimore, MD 21215
About:
Join us each Wednesday to strengthen relationships and explore post-high school pathways. Get in-person Thread Family planning & support.
Who should attend?
Open to all Thread young people and volunteers looking for programming, resources, activities, and partners to support post high school pathways and plans.
How do I support?
You can RSVP in advance using the links below, or just show up (bring other volunteers and young people with you!) If you like having a specific role you can sign ahead of time
here
, or just ask for a role when you get to the check-in table!!!
November Focus: Check In, Stay Connected, Keep Moving Forward!
November is here, and our post-high-school young people are settling into
new jobs, college classes, training programs, and Maryland Corps / Service Year placements!
With the excitement of new beginnings behind us, now is the time to check in, see how things are really going, and make sure young people have the support they need to keep moving forward.
Each Wednesday at TouchPoint
threadHOURS
, young people can connect with staff, volunteers, and resource partners to troubleshoot challenges, access resources, and take their next steps. Whether they're struggling with a new placement, navigating college or work, facing financial pressures, or figuring out what's next, threadHOURS is a place to get support and keep building momentum.
As
Maryland Corps / Service Year applications wrap up
, our focus is shifting from getting young people into opportunities to
helping them succeed once they're there!
And with the holiday season approaching, it's an especially important time to stay connected, celebrate progress, and catch challenges before they become bigger barriers.
How you can roll as a volunteer:
This month, make the check-in count!
Reach out to your young person and ask how things are
really
going. Are they feeling good about school, work, or Service Year? What's going well? What's getting in the way? Are there any concerns or needs that might become more pressing as the holidays approach?
Don't just check the box — help connect the dots!
Celebrate their wins, listen for challenges, and make sure any concerns get elevated to Thread staff so we can help address them. Better yet, come to threadHOURS together and turn those conversations into action.
Your consistency, encouragement, and follow-through can make all the difference!

Maryland Blockchain Association & CryptoMondays Virtual Meetup

Network virtually with those located in the DMV (District of Columbia, Virginia & Maryland) and internationally!

This monthly Monday meeting is hosted by Maryland Blockchain Association, Blockchain Legal Institute, and Blockchain Legal Institute Foundation.

The Maryland Blockchain Association is the Maryland Chapter Lead for CryptoMondays. The MDBA's monthly virtual networking event is hosted monthly on the 1st Monday of each month. If you are interested in establishing a meetup in alliance with the MDBA and CryptoMondays please reach out.

The Maryland Blockchain Association is a trade association dedicated to representing the innovative tech community within Maryland to provide education, economic development and outreach to those within our local community.

CryptoMondays is a decentralized global community that brings together individuals passionate about cryptocurrency and blockchain technology.

The Blockchain Legal Institute is a centralized library of decentralized resources & the only Institute specifically dedicated to help provide continuing education to lawyers, compliance officers, business professionals and those learning about digital assets.

The Blockchain Legal Institute Foundation is a non profit dedicated to developing digital asset educational resources for consumers and families.

Learn about the latest trends in digital currency and blockchain technology, and gain insights into the world of crypto-tokens, Bitcoin, Ethereum as well as updates involving the regulations impacting consumers and businesses within our world of blockchain, IoT, RWA, artificial intelligence, and innovative technology. Expert speakers will cover blockchain security, cryptography, and other relevant topics in the fast-evolving cryptocurrency market.

Whether you are a seasoned investor or new to the world of virtual currency, these virtual events are the perfect opportunity to network locally and internationally with like-minded individuals and expand your knowledge in the realm of enterprise blockchain technology.

Don't miss out on this chance to stay ahead of the curve and explore the exciting opportunities that cryptocurrency and blockchain technology have to offer.

Join us each Wednesday to strengthen relationships and explore post-high school pathways. Get in-person Thread Family planning & support.
Who should attend?
Open to all Thread young people and volunteers looking for programming, resources, activities, and partners to support post high school pathways and plans.
How do I support?

November Focus: Check In, Stay Connected, Keep Moving Forward!
November is here, and our post-high-school young people are settling into
new jobs, college classes, training programs, and Maryland Corps / Service Year placements!
With the excitement of new beginnings behind us, now is the time to check in, see how things are really going, and make sure young people have the support they need to keep moving forward.
Each Wednesday at TouchPoint
threadHOURS
, young people can connect with staff, volunteers, and resource partners to troubleshoot challenges, access resources, and take their next steps. Whether they're struggling with a new placement, navigating college or work, facing financial pressures, or figuring out what's next, threadHOURS is a place to get support and keep building momentum.
As
Maryland Corps / Service Year applications wrap up
, our focus is shifting from getting young people into opportunities to
helping them succeed once they're there!
And with the holiday season approaching, it's an especially important time to stay connected, celebrate progress, and catch challenges before they become bigger barriers.
How you can roll as a volunteer:
This month, make the check-in count!
Reach out to your young person and ask how things are
really
going. Are they feeling good about school, work, or Service Year? What's going well? What's getting in the way? Are there any concerns or needs that might become more pressing as the holidays approach?
Don't just check the box — help connect the dots!
Celebrate their wins, listen for challenges, and make sure any concerns get elevated to Thread staff so we can help address them. Better yet, come to threadHOURS together and turn those conversations into action.
Your consistency, encouragement, and follow-through can make all the difference!

\~ Embracing a Healthier, Sustainable, Compassionate and Peaceful Way of Eating and Living \~

**Baltimore Veg/Vegan Meetup** group is warm and welcoming. We host monthly Veg/Vegan restaurant gatherings, and invite all who are interested in moving toward a healthier, earth-friendly diet and lifestyle.

Our group members enjoy the food and atmosphere of **Taj Palace**, 9419 Common Brook Rd, Owings Mills, MD, 21117, which has a large private room that's perfect for our discussions. The buffet at Taj Palace is just $22, and features a good number of vegan and veg options. The waitstaff is friendly and helpful with questions.

Discussion topics: You’re invited to tell us a little about yourself and what got you interested in veg/vegan/plant-based ideals and lifestyle. Feel free to share a success story, inspiration or announcement. You are also free to open or suggest a topic for discussion.

One topic that often comes up:
"Someone or something that gives you hope for a better world?"

Micah Johnson: "Aku: Battle For Pyra"

Aku, space traveler of the metaverse, is BACK and ready to blast off in book two of this action-packed sci-fi series, where he and his friends must travel to a fiery planet to recover a gem of untold power, lest it fall into the wrong hands.

After saving the planet Ibra from a ruthless space militia, Aku is ready for a break. But when his grandfather announces an urgent mission to the fiery, lava-filled planet Pyra, Aku and his friends end up on their most dangerous mission yet.

What awaits them is a world forged in lava and legend. Here, ancient beings guard the GEM: a radiant core said to control the light of the universe. To claim the GEM, Aku’s crew must survive three deadly trials—racing through molten mazes, battling in a gravity-defying magmaball arena, and descending into the planet’s core itself—before Aku comes face-to-face with his greatest enemy…and the truth about his family’s past.

Filled with humor and high-octane twists, this is a cosmic coming-of-age story about courage, legacy, and the value of finding your winning team.

About the Author:

Micah Johnson is a former Major League Baseball player turned artist, is the creator of the phenomenon that is Aku, a 3D animated boy wearing an oversized astronaut helmet. Micah’s fine art piece catapulted him from retired athlete to creator of the 2020 NFT of the Year. Aku: Journey to Ibra is Aku’s origin story and Micah’s first book. He lives in Maine with his wife and daughters.

About the Program:

To attend in person please register here. Doors will open to registered attendees at 3 pm. All registered in person attendees will receive a free copy of the book while supplies last. Free street parking and bike parking are available.

10:30 PM
Save the Date: DefenseTech in Harford County

Some of the most important defense innovation in the county is happening right here in our region, and it's time we talked about it. UpSurge Baltimore & GBC are bringing together the people building the future of defense and national security on Tuesday, January 19, 2027, for an evening of conversation, connection, and collaboration at the CONVERGE Innovation Center. CONVERGE helps startups bring biomanufacturing technologies developed at Aberdeen Proving Ground (APG) to market and trains the workforce that will power them, which makes it the right place to start this conversation. The evening will focus on the breakthrough work coming out of APG, the unique challenges defense-sector companies face, where the region's biggest opportunities lie, and how our entrepreneurial ecosystem can step up to support the companies working in this space. You'll be in the room with innovators, technologists, workforce development experts, elected officials, Department of War officials, and the anchor institutions shaping the region's defense and national security future. Together, we'll build the partnerships and shared commitment that will position the Greater Baltimore Region to lead in this field. Register and mark your calendar now. The full program, speaker lineup, and additional details will be announced in the coming months. Stay tuned. You won't want to miss this one.

CONVERGE Innovation Center, 1201 Technology Drive, Aberdeen, MD, 21001

threadHOURS® at TouchPoint - Ongoing

Every Wednesday | 3-6 pm
Location:
TouchPoint: 3201 Tioga Parkway, Suite P, Baltimore, MD 21215
About:
Join us each Wednesday to strengthen relationships and explore post-high school pathways. Get in-person Thread Family planning & support.
Who should attend?
Open to all Thread young people and volunteers looking for programming, resources, activities, and partners to support post high school pathways and plans.
How do I support?
You can RSVP in advance using the links below, or just show up (bring other volunteers and young people with you!) If you like having a specific role you can sign ahead of time
here
, or just ask for a role when you get to the check-in table!!!
November Focus: Check In, Stay Connected, Keep Moving Forward!
November is here, and our post-high-school young people are settling into
new jobs, college classes, training programs, and Maryland Corps / Service Year placements!
With the excitement of new beginnings behind us, now is the time to check in, see how things are really going, and make sure young people have the support they need to keep moving forward.
Each Wednesday at TouchPoint
threadHOURS
, young people can connect with staff, volunteers, and resource partners to troubleshoot challenges, access resources, and take their next steps. Whether they're struggling with a new placement, navigating college or work, facing financial pressures, or figuring out what's next, threadHOURS is a place to get support and keep building momentum.
As
Maryland Corps / Service Year applications wrap up
, our focus is shifting from getting young people into opportunities to
helping them succeed once they're there!
And with the holiday season approaching, it's an especially important time to stay connected, celebrate progress, and catch challenges before they become bigger barriers.
How you can roll as a volunteer:
This month, make the check-in count!
Reach out to your young person and ask how things are
really
going. Are they feeling good about school, work, or Service Year? What's going well? What's getting in the way? Are there any concerns or needs that might become more pressing as the holidays approach?
Don't just check the box — help connect the dots!
Celebrate their wins, listen for challenges, and make sure any concerns get elevated to Thread staff so we can help address them. Better yet, come to threadHOURS together and turn those conversations into action.
Your consistency, encouragement, and follow-through can make all the difference!

threadHOURS® at TouchPoint - Ongoing

Every Wednesday | 3-6 pm
Location:
TouchPoint: 3201 Tioga Parkway, Suite P, Baltimore, MD 21215
About:
Join us each Wednesday to strengthen relationships and explore post-high school pathways. Get in-person Thread Family planning & support.
Who should attend?
Open to all Thread young people and volunteers looking for programming, resources, activities, and partners to support post high school pathways and plans.
How do I support?
You can RSVP in advance using the links below, or just show up (bring other volunteers and young people with you!) If you like having a specific role you can sign ahead of time
here
, or just ask for a role when you get to the check-in table!!!
November Focus: Check In, Stay Connected, Keep Moving Forward!
November is here, and our post-high-school young people are settling into
new jobs, college classes, training programs, and Maryland Corps / Service Year placements!
With the excitement of new beginnings behind us, now is the time to check in, see how things are really going, and make sure young people have the support they need to keep moving forward.
Each Wednesday at TouchPoint
threadHOURS
, young people can connect with staff, volunteers, and resource partners to troubleshoot challenges, access resources, and take their next steps. Whether they're struggling with a new placement, navigating college or work, facing financial pressures, or figuring out what's next, threadHOURS is a place to get support and keep building momentum.
As
Maryland Corps / Service Year applications wrap up
, our focus is shifting from getting young people into opportunities to
helping them succeed once they're there!
And with the holiday season approaching, it's an especially important time to stay connected, celebrate progress, and catch challenges before they become bigger barriers.
How you can roll as a volunteer:
This month, make the check-in count!
Reach out to your young person and ask how things are
really
going. Are they feeling good about school, work, or Service Year? What's going well? What's getting in the way? Are there any concerns or needs that might become more pressing as the holidays approach?
Don't just check the box — help connect the dots!
Celebrate their wins, listen for challenges, and make sure any concerns get elevated to Thread staff so we can help address them. Better yet, come to threadHOURS together and turn those conversations into action.
Your consistency, encouragement, and follow-through can make all the difference!

Find a Startup to Help or Join

**Welcome!**

The official registration page is [here](Startupoasisvirtual.eventbrite.com).

If you are a developer, UX designer, marketer, or anyone else in the tech ecosystem looking to join or help a tech startup, or even just get involved in a project, this event is for you!

We will be introducing projects for you to get involved with during the pitches. There is no group like this on Meetup or in the startup world because we filter out the BS and get you going on a project ASAP.

(Stay inside the Startup Oasis by joining our [newsletter](https://mailchi.mp/startupoasis/meetup)!)

What happens first in the event is startup founders pitch their business or idea to the audience, which is full of the developers, designers, marketers, etc.

If you are interested in one of the projects / startups, you can join one of the founders in a breakout room to continue building, workshopping, and/or onboarding the startup with attendees.

People have been able to start and advance their businesses as a result of this process.

We are meeting on Zoom, the link is here in the listing.

**Agenda:**
**Intros:** During the first 10 minutes, we will give you the history, structure, and future plans of Startup Oasis and open signups for founders that want to pitch their startups.

**Pitches:** Each founder will then get up to 3 minutes to pitch their startup. This format is recommended: name, business, the problem, your solution, target customer base, and your biggest challenge/current need. This part is similar to Shark Tank.

**Breakout Groups:** For the remainder of the event, each founder gets a breakout room, and you can talk to the founders in greater detail about their needs and challenges in a small group setting. This part is similar to a hackathon.

Startup Oasis was created to pierce the illusion of accessibility of startups and tech by creating a grassroots forum for early-stage founders to pitch to those in the tech ecosystem to get real-time feedback for their idea or business.

Use this [link](https://lnk.bio/startup.oasis) to:

* Follow us on LinkedIn
* Join our community on Discord
* Donate to our cause
* Visit our website

**FAQ:**
**Is this event free to attend?** Yes - Startup Oasis will always be free for anyone to attend. If you would like to donate, you can do so directly on our [website](https://donate.stripe.com/eVa2a0dV27Nlb2ofYY). You can also talk to us about volunteer or sponsorship opportunities.

**How do I sign up to pitch?** RSVP here. Right when the event starts, fill out the form and then raise your hand on Zoom. That will also determine the order. You can also buy a VIP ticket to support our cause and guarantee you a spot to pitch. To be eligible to pitch, you must be the cofounder of a technology-based startup. Agencies, consultants, coaches, MLM schemes, and nonprofits are not eligible to pitch, but you can still watch the pitches and join the breakouts.

**What happens after the pitches?** The breakout groups open for the remainder of the event. Each founder gets a breakout room, and you can talk more about their business and needs with them.

**Can I invite other people that I know?** Yes - please have them RSVP here or on the [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/startup-oasis-global) event listing.

**How do I get the most out of this event?**

* Founders - In this event, no money is awarded nor are any winners named. We are not here to critique your pitch, just to help you find teammates, cofounders, and feedback from other professionals. Make sure your pitch is 3 minutes or less and clear about what your biggest needs are.
* Attendees - If you are new to startups and tech, feel free to just watch with no pressure to participate. If you are looking to join a startup or find a side project, make sure you take notes during the pitches to join the group of the founder that you're most interested in helping. Most founders need help with either developing the product or with a go-to-market strategy.
*

**Do we meet in person?** We do this event in Atlanta, GA each month in Midtown at ATDC.

**Content:** We are looking for founders to be interviewed or people to interview founders for short videos. Let us know if you are interested!

Maryland Blockchain Association & CryptoMondays Virtual Meetup

Network virtually with those located in the DMV (District of Columbia, Virginia & Maryland) and internationally!

This monthly Monday meeting is hosted by Maryland Blockchain Association, Blockchain Legal Institute, and Blockchain Legal Institute Foundation.

The Maryland Blockchain Association is the Maryland Chapter Lead for CryptoMondays. The MDBA's monthly virtual networking event is hosted monthly on the 1st Monday of each month. If you are interested in establishing a meetup in alliance with the MDBA and CryptoMondays please reach out.

The Maryland Blockchain Association is a trade association dedicated to representing the innovative tech community within Maryland to provide education, economic development and outreach to those within our local community.

CryptoMondays is a decentralized global community that brings together individuals passionate about cryptocurrency and blockchain technology.

The Blockchain Legal Institute is a centralized library of decentralized resources & the only Institute specifically dedicated to help provide continuing education to lawyers, compliance officers, business professionals and those learning about digital assets.

The Blockchain Legal Institute Foundation is a non profit dedicated to developing digital asset educational resources for consumers and families.

Learn about the latest trends in digital currency and blockchain technology, and gain insights into the world of crypto-tokens, Bitcoin, Ethereum as well as updates involving the regulations impacting consumers and businesses within our world of blockchain, IoT, RWA, artificial intelligence, and innovative technology. Expert speakers will cover blockchain security, cryptography, and other relevant topics in the fast-evolving cryptocurrency market.

Whether you are a seasoned investor or new to the world of virtual currency, these virtual events are the perfect opportunity to network locally and internationally with like-minded individuals and expand your knowledge in the realm of enterprise blockchain technology.

Don't miss out on this chance to stay ahead of the curve and explore the exciting opportunities that cryptocurrency and blockchain technology have to offer.

About:
Join us each Wednesday to strengthen relationships and explore post-high school pathways. Get in-person Thread Family planning & support.
Who should attend?
Open to all Thread young people and volunteers looking for programming, resources, activities, and partners to support post high school pathways and plans.
How do I support?
You can RSVP in advance using the links below, or just show up (bring other volunteers and young people with you!) If you like having a specific role you can sign ahead of time
here
, or just ask for a role when you get to the check-in table!!!
November Focus: Check In, Stay Connected, Keep Moving Forward!
November is here, and our post-high-school young people are settling into
new jobs, college classes, training programs, and Maryland Corps / Service Year placements!
With the excitement of new beginnings behind us, now is the time to check in, see how things are really going, and make sure young people have the support they need to keep moving forward.
Each Wednesday at TouchPoint
threadHOURS
, young people can connect with staff, volunteers, and resource partners to troubleshoot challenges, access resources, and take their next steps. Whether they're struggling with a new placement, navigating college or work, facing financial pressures, or figuring out what's next, threadHOURS is a place to get support and keep building momentum.
As
Maryland Corps / Service Year applications wrap up
, our focus is shifting from getting young people into opportunities to
helping them succeed once they're there!
And with the holiday season approaching, it's an especially important time to stay connected, celebrate progress, and catch challenges before they become bigger barriers.
How you can roll as a volunteer:
This month, make the check-in count!
Reach out to your young person and ask how things are
really
going. Are they feeling good about school, work, or Service Year? What's going well? What's getting in the way? Are there any concerns or needs that might become more pressing as the holidays approach?
Don't just check the box — help connect the dots!
Celebrate their wins, listen for challenges, and make sure any concerns get elevated to Thread staff so we can help address them. Better yet, come to threadHOURS together and turn those conversations into action.
Your consistency, encouragement, and follow-through can make all the difference!

Location:

About:
Join us each Wednesday to strengthen relationships and explore post-high school pathways. Get in-person Thread Family planning & support.
Who should attend?
Open to all Thread young people and volunteers looking for programming, resources, activities, and partners to support post high school pathways and plans.
How do I support?
You can RSVP in advance using the links below, or just show up (bring other volunteers and young people with you!) If you like having a specific role you can sign ahead of time
here
, or just ask for a role when you get to the check-in table!!!
November Focus: Check In, Stay Connected, Keep Moving Forward!
November is here, and our post-high-school young people are settling into
new jobs, college classes, training programs, and Maryland Corps / Service Year placements!
With the excitement of new beginnings behind us, now is the time to check in, see how things are really going, and make sure young people have the support they need to keep moving forward.
Each Wednesday at TouchPoint
threadHOURS
, young people can connect with staff, volunteers, and resource partners to troubleshoot challenges, access resources, and take their next steps. Whether they're struggling with a new placement, navigating college or work, facing financial pressures, or figuring out what's next, threadHOURS is a place to get support and keep building momentum.
As
Maryland Corps / Service Year applications wrap up
, our focus is shifting from getting young people into opportunities to
helping them succeed once they're there!
And with the holiday season approaching, it's an especially important time to stay connected, celebrate progress, and catch challenges before they become bigger barriers.
How you can roll as a volunteer:
This month, make the check-in count!
Reach out to your young person and ask how things are
really
going. Are they feeling good about school, work, or Service Year? What's going well? What's getting in the way? Are there any concerns or needs that might become more pressing as the holidays approach?
Don't just check the box — help connect the dots!
Celebrate their wins, listen for challenges, and make sure any concerns get elevated to Thread staff so we can help address them. Better yet, come to threadHOURS together and turn those conversations into action.
Your consistency, encouragement, and follow-through can make all the difference!

Hosted by the Alliance for the Chesapeake Bay and Penn State Extension, the
So You Want To Grow…
Webinar Series is for anyone who wants to learn how to grow native trees and shrubs.
Topics to Be Covered
Each webinar will highlight different native tree or shrub species and include technical information on methods for germinating seeds and growing seedlings for conservation projects or your own backyard! Attendees will learn how to identify native trees and shrubs, their ecology, when and how to harvest their seeds for propagation, and the benefits that these plants provide to the ecosystem.
You don’t need to be a seasoned grower or have a greenhouse to grow native trees and shrubs!

Find a Startup to Help or Join

**Welcome!**

The official registration page is [here](Startupoasisvirtual.eventbrite.com).

If you are a developer, UX designer, marketer, or anyone else in the tech ecosystem looking to join or help a tech startup, or even just get involved in a project, this event is for you!

We will be introducing projects for you to get involved with during the pitches. There is no group like this on Meetup or in the startup world because we filter out the BS and get you going on a project ASAP.

(Stay inside the Startup Oasis by joining our [newsletter](https://mailchi.mp/startupoasis/meetup)!)

What happens first in the event is startup founders pitch their business or idea to the audience, which is full of the developers, designers, marketers, etc.

If you are interested in one of the projects / startups, you can join one of the founders in a breakout room to continue building, workshopping, and/or onboarding the startup with attendees.

People have been able to start and advance their businesses as a result of this process.

We are meeting on Zoom, the link is here in the listing.

**Agenda:**
**Intros:** During the first 10 minutes, we will give you the history, structure, and future plans of Startup Oasis and open signups for founders that want to pitch their startups.

**Pitches:** Each founder will then get up to 3 minutes to pitch their startup. This format is recommended: name, business, the problem, your solution, target customer base, and your biggest challenge/current need. This part is similar to Shark Tank.

**Breakout Groups:** For the remainder of the event, each founder gets a breakout room, and you can talk to the founders in greater detail about their needs and challenges in a small group setting. This part is similar to a hackathon.

Startup Oasis was created to pierce the illusion of accessibility of startups and tech by creating a grassroots forum for early-stage founders to pitch to those in the tech ecosystem to get real-time feedback for their idea or business.

Use this [link](https://lnk.bio/startup.oasis) to:

* Follow us on LinkedIn
* Join our community on Discord
* Donate to our cause
* Visit our website

**FAQ:**
**Is this event free to attend?** Yes - Startup Oasis will always be free for anyone to attend. If you would like to donate, you can do so directly on our [website](https://donate.stripe.com/eVa2a0dV27Nlb2ofYY). You can also talk to us about volunteer or sponsorship opportunities.

**How do I sign up to pitch?** RSVP here. Right when the event starts, fill out the form and then raise your hand on Zoom. That will also determine the order. You can also buy a VIP ticket to support our cause and guarantee you a spot to pitch. To be eligible to pitch, you must be the cofounder of a technology-based startup. Agencies, consultants, coaches, MLM schemes, and nonprofits are not eligible to pitch, but you can still watch the pitches and join the breakouts.

**What happens after the pitches?** The breakout groups open for the remainder of the event. Each founder gets a breakout room, and you can talk more about their business and needs with them.

**Can I invite other people that I know?** Yes - please have them RSVP here or on the [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/startup-oasis-global) event listing.

**How do I get the most out of this event?**

* Founders - In this event, no money is awarded nor are any winners named. We are not here to critique your pitch, just to help you find teammates, cofounders, and feedback from other professionals. Make sure your pitch is 3 minutes or less and clear about what your biggest needs are.
* Attendees - If you are new to startups and tech, feel free to just watch with no pressure to participate. If you are looking to join a startup or find a side project, make sure you take notes during the pitches to join the group of the founder that you're most interested in helping. Most founders need help with either developing the product or with a go-to-market strategy.
*

**Do we meet in person?** We do this event in Atlanta, GA each month in Midtown at ATDC.

**Content:** We are looking for founders to be interviewed or people to interview founders for short videos. Let us know if you are interested!

Kate Messner: "Keep the Ghost Light On"

A haunted Broadway theater.
A ghost demanding justice.
Three kids who must follow the clues to unlock the past . . .

When Daphne, Luna, and Felix break into a shuttered theater to produce their own musical, they find it haunted by the ghost of an angry showgirl who makes a cryptic demand:

TRUTH

Daphne is already struggling with her own truth, ever since a cute older boy humiliated her in front of the drama club last spring. Now her heart is full of secrets, and she hasn't written a new song in months.

But the ghost is persistent, and the friends find themselves sleuthing through empty research libraries and abandoned theaters in a search for answers. As the hauntings escalate from spooky to deadly, can they uncover the truth of what happened a century ago and finally free their ghosts?

Told via stage play, song lyrics, letters, and more this fast-paced, accessible novel will capture any reader.

About the Author:

Kate Messner is a former middle-school English teacher and the author of E. B. White Read Aloud Award winner The Brilliant Fall of Gianna Z. and its companion, The Exact Location of Home; Sugar and Ice; Eye of the Storm; Wake Up Missing; All the Answers; The Seventh Wish; Capture the Flag; Hide and Seek; the Marty McGuire chapter book series; the Ranger in Time chapter book series; and several picture books. She lives on Lake Champlain with her husband and two kids. When she’s not reading or writing, she loves hiking, kayaking, biking, and watching thunderstorms over the lake. Visit her website at www.katemessner.com.

Network virtually with those located in the DMV (District of Columbia, Virginia & Maryland) and internationally!

This monthly Monday meeting is hosted by Maryland Blockchain Association, Blockchain Legal Institute, and Blockchain Legal Institute Foundation.

The Maryland Blockchain Association is the Maryland Chapter Lead for CryptoMondays. The MDBA's monthly virtual networking event is hosted monthly on the 1st Monday of each month. If you are interested in establishing a meetup in alliance with the MDBA and CryptoMondays please reach out.

The Maryland Blockchain Association is a trade association dedicated to representing the innovative tech community within Maryland to provide education, economic development and outreach to those within our local community.

CryptoMondays is a decentralized global community that brings together individuals passionate about cryptocurrency and blockchain technology.

The Blockchain Legal Institute is a centralized library of decentralized resources & the only Institute specifically dedicated to help provide continuing education to lawyers, compliance officers, business professionals and those learning about digital assets.

The Blockchain Legal Institute Foundation is a non profit dedicated to developing digital asset educational resources for consumers and families.

Learn about the latest trends in digital currency and blockchain technology, and gain insights into the world of crypto-tokens, Bitcoin, Ethereum as well as updates involving the regulations impacting consumers and businesses within our world of blockchain, IoT, RWA, artificial intelligence, and innovative technology. Expert speakers will cover blockchain security, cryptography, and other relevant topics in the fast-evolving cryptocurrency market.

Whether you are a seasoned investor or new to the world of virtual currency, these virtual events are the perfect opportunity to network locally and internationally with like-minded individuals and expand your knowledge in the realm of enterprise blockchain technology.

Don't miss out on this chance to stay ahead of the curve and explore the exciting opportunities that cryptocurrency and blockchain technology have to offer.

threadHOURS® at TouchPoint - Ongoing

Every Wednesday | 3-6 pm
Location:
TouchPoint: 3201 Tioga Parkway, Suite P, Baltimore, MD 21215
About:
Join us each Wednesday to strengthen relationships and explore post-high school pathways. Get in-person Thread Family planning & support.
Who should attend?
Open to all Thread young people and volunteers looking for programming, resources, activities, and partners to support post high school pathways and plans.
How do I support?
You can RSVP in advance using the links below, or just show up (bring other volunteers and young people with you!) If you like having a specific role you can sign ahead of time
here
, or just ask for a role when you get to the check-in table!!!
November Focus: Check In, Stay Connected, Keep Moving Forward!
November is here, and our post-high-school young people are settling into
new jobs, college classes, training programs, and Maryland Corps / Service Year placements!
With the excitement of new beginnings behind us, now is the time to check in, see how things are really going, and make sure young people have the support they need to keep moving forward.
Each Wednesday at TouchPoint
threadHOURS
, young people can connect with staff, volunteers, and resource partners to troubleshoot challenges, access resources, and take their next steps. Whether they're struggling with a new placement, navigating college or work, facing financial pressures, or figuring out what's next, threadHOURS is a place to get support and keep building momentum.
As
Maryland Corps / Service Year applications wrap up
, our focus is shifting from getting young people into opportunities to
helping them succeed once they're there!
And with the holiday season approaching, it's an especially important time to stay connected, celebrate progress, and catch challenges before they become bigger barriers.
How you can roll as a volunteer:
This month, make the check-in count!
Reach out to your young person and ask how things are
really
going. Are they feeling good about school, work, or Service Year? What's going well? What's getting in the way? Are there any concerns or needs that might become more pressing as the holidays approach?
Don't just check the box — help connect the dots!
Celebrate their wins, listen for challenges, and make sure any concerns get elevated to Thread staff so we can help address them. Better yet, come to threadHOURS together and turn those conversations into action.
Your consistency, encouragement, and follow-through can make all the difference!

We also launch our own climate-related actions.</p><p><b>Mission Statement: </b></p><p>Our purpose is to work together to improve the health and legacy of Washington DC communities—human and nonhuman alike—by undertaking local campaigns that reverse or prevent climate change and the inequity arising from it. We welcome those who want to organize and build power to address the climate crisis, to live more harmoniously with the environment, and to pass on a liveable planet to generations to come.</p>

So You Want to Grow Trees from Seed: A Webinar Series, Maples

Hosted by the Alliance for the Chesapeake Bay and Penn State Extension, the
So You Want To Grow…
Webinar Series is for anyone who wants to learn how to grow native trees and shrubs.
Topics to Be Covered
Each webinar will highlight different native tree or shrub species and include technical information on methods for germinating seeds and growing seedlings for conservation projects or your own backyard! Attendees will learn how to identify native trees and shrubs, their ecology, when and how to harvest their seeds for propagation, and the benefits that these plants provide to the ecosystem.
You don’t need to be a seasoned grower or have a greenhouse to grow native trees and shrubs!
This webinar series is free to attend. Please register using the links below.
